Definition: to sever, i.e. ransom; gener. to release, preserve
BiblicalUsage: Pâdâh is to ransom, to redeem, to rescue by paying a price. The firstborn is redeemed, Israel is redeemed out of the house of bondmen because the LORD loved them, the psalmist trusts God will redeem his soul from the power of the grave, and Hosea hears God say, I will ransom them from the power of the grave.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe redemption is never cheap talk in this word. Something is paid, someone is bought back, and the buyer is always the LORD Himself.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea
